paper.title_en: Charge-activated birefringence of an Einstein-tensor-coupled vector field on Reissner--Nordström black holes
paper.abstract_en: We study the propagation of a neutral vector test field non-minimally coupled to the Einstein tensor on a Reissner--Nordström black hole. The interaction vanishes on a vacuum background, so electric charge is required to activate the curvature-induced response. The parity potentials have one symmetry: reversing the sign of the coupling exchanges the electric and magnetic susceptibilities. Because of this symmetry, the two polarizations respond identically at first order in the coupling. The dominant propagation-level effect is therefore a common shift of the effective photon sphere and of the shadow radius, not a birefringent splitting. The variation of shadow size can mimic the charge variation of a black hole. When the coupling is weak, polarization splitting appears only in the second-order term, distinguishing this interaction from corrections involving only charge. We follow this ordering through full-frequency absorption and scattering, the semiclassical glory, and ray-traced double shadows. The absorption parity asymmetry and the shadow rim splitting probe the difference between the effective potentials. The polarization-summed backward scattering isolates the helicity-reversing response, which is zero without the coupling. At the positive-coupling boundary the splitting grows but stays finite. Beyond it the even-parity potential has a pole outside the horizon. In the high-multipole limit, the two boundaries of the stability window both correspond to the thresholds of bound-state instability, but their physical properties differ: the negatively coupled boundary forms a regular potential well, while the positively coupled boundary marks the breaking of regularity. A Frobenius analysis shows a forced logarithmic branch at that pole. Without an additional physical connection condition, the continuation across the pole is not unique.
